name: Ball Python – Normal (Classic)
short_description: A calm, captive-bred classic ball python hatchling with rich chocolate and gold banding — the ideal first snake.
long_description:

## Care summary

- **Scientific name:** *Python regius*
- **Care level:** Beginner
- **Adult size:** 3–5 ft (90–150 cm)
- **Lifespan:** 25–30+ years

Ball pythons may fast in winter. A healthy adult skipping a few meals is normal — track weight with a gram scale rather than worrying about missed feeds.

name: High Yellow Leopard Gecko
short_description: A captive-bred high yellow leopard gecko with a bright golden body and bold black spots, eating dubia roaches and ready for its first home.
long_description:
The high yellow leopard gecko is the morph most people picture when they think of a pet gecko: a bright golden-yellow body, crisp black spotting and a banded tail that fades to soft spots with age. It is one of the oldest selectively bred leopard gecko morphs and still one of the most popular, because it combines striking color with the hardy, easy-going nature that makes leopard geckos such good first reptiles.

## Why keepers choose a high yellow

- **Beginner friendly:** calm, slow-moving and rarely bites once settled.
- **Manageable size:** adults reach 7–10 in (18–25 cm), so a 36×18×18 in enclosure is plenty.
- **Long-lived:** with good care, high yellow leopard geckos often live 15–20 years.
- **Great value:** the classic yellow look at a fraction of the price of designer morphs.

Every gecko we sell is captive bred, has eaten at least six meals with us and is weighed before shipping. Juveniles are typically 3–5 months old.

## Setting up for a high yellow leopard gecko

Give your gecko a warm side with a basking surface of 88–92°F (31–33°C), a cool side around 72–78°F (22–26°C) and three hides: warm, cool and humid. A low-level UVB tube and a halogen basking bulb on a dimming thermostat recreate the gentle sunlight and warm rocks of its native grasslands. Our [Leopard Gecko Complete Starter Kit](/shop/enclosures/leopard-gecko-starter-kit) bundles everything, and our [leopard gecko care guide](/blog/leopard-gecko-care-guide) walks through each step.

## Feeding

High yellows are insectivores. Offer gut-loaded dubia roaches, crickets or black soldier fly larvae daily for juveniles and every two to three days for adults, lightly dusted with calcium with D3. Hornworms and mealworms make good occasional treats.

## Color and genetics

High yellow is a line-bred trait rather than a single gene, so color intensity varies between animals and often deepens as the gecko matures. Hatchlings are banded; adult spotting develops over the first year.

## Frequently asked questions

### How big do high yellow leopard geckos get?

Adults usually reach 7–10 in (18–25 cm) from nose to tail tip and weigh 45–80 g. Size depends on genetics, diet and sex, with males usually a little larger.

### Is a high yellow leopard gecko good for beginners?

Yes. High yellows have the same calm temperament and simple care as normal leopard geckos, so they are an excellent first reptile for responsible teens and adults.

### Do high yellow leopard geckos need UVB?

They can survive without it if they get dietary vitamin D3, but most keepers and vets now recommend low-level UVB (5–6%) with plenty of shade, because it supports natural behavior and bone health.

### What do high yellow leopard geckos eat?

Live insects only: dubia roaches, crickets and black soldier fly larvae as staples, with hornworms and mealworms as treats. Dust insects with calcium and give a multivitamin weekly.

name: Tremper Albino Leopard Gecko
short_description: A captive-bred Tremper albino leopard gecko in warm yellow, peach and lavender tones with light eyes. Calm, feeding well and beginner friendly.
long_description:
The Tremper albino leopard gecko is the most widely kept albino leopard gecko strain, prized for its soft yellow, peach and lavender coloring with light caramel to brown markings instead of black. It is a simple recessive gene, first established in the 1990s, and it appears in many of the most popular combination morphs today. A Tremper albino on its own is an affordable, eye-catching gecko with the same easy care as any leopard gecko.

## What makes an albino leopard gecko different

- **Coloring:** albinos lack black pigment, so their spots and bands show as brown or lavender on a yellow or cream base.
- **Eyes:** light-colored eyes that are more sensitive to bright light than a normal gecko's.
- **Temperament:** the same calm, handleable nature as other leopard geckos.
- **Genetics:** Tremper, Bell and Rainwater albinos are separate genes and not compatible with each other. This is a Tremper albino.

## Light sensitivity

Because albino leopard geckos are more light sensitive, give them extra shade. Use a modest basking bulb, place hides on both sides and make sure any UVB covers only part of the enclosure so the gecko can choose its exposure. Many keepers use a 5% tube rather than anything stronger for albinos.

## Housing and care

Provide a 36×18×18 in enclosure with a warm basking surface of 88–92°F (31–33°C), a cool side of 72–78°F (22–26°C) and warm, cool and humid hides. Our [leopard gecko care guide](/blog/leopard-gecko-care-guide) covers temperatures, substrate and handling step by step, and the [Leopard Gecko Complete Starter Kit](/shop/enclosures/leopard-gecko-starter-kit) puts the whole setup in one box.

## Diet

Feed gut-loaded live insects such as dubia roaches and crickets, dusted with calcium. Juveniles eat daily, adults every two to three days. Our albinos are established on insects before they ship.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do albino leopard geckos have vision problems?

Their eyes are more sensitive to bright light, but they see well enough to hunt and live normal lives. Providing shade and avoiding very bright lighting keeps them comfortable.

### What is the difference between Tremper, Bell and Rainwater albino?

They are three separate recessive albino genes discovered by different breeders. They look slightly different and are not compatible, so breeding a Tremper to a Bell albino produces normal-looking offspring.

### How long do albino leopard geckos live?

The same as other leopard geckos: commonly 15–20 years with good care, correct temperatures and a varied, supplemented insect diet.

name: Leatherback Bearded Dragon
short_description: A captive-bred leatherback bearded dragon with reduced, smooth back scales and vivid color. Hand-raised, eating greens and insects.
long_description:
The leatherback bearded dragon is one of the most popular bearded dragon morphs, known for its noticeably smoother back. The leatherback gene reduces the size of the spiky scales along the dragon's back, giving it a sleek, leathery feel while keeping the classic bearded dragon spikes on the sides and beard. Smoother scales also make colors look brighter, so leatherbacks often show more vivid orange, red or yellow than standard-scaled dragons.

## Leatherback genetics

Leatherback is an incomplete dominant trait. One copy produces the leatherback look; two copies produce a "silkback", which has no scales at all and needs much more specialized care. We sell leatherbacks only, which keep enough skin protection for normal husbandry.

## Why choose a leatherback bearded dragon

- **Personable:** bearded dragons are curious, active by day and among the most interactive pet reptiles.
- **Striking look:** smoother scales and stronger color than a normal dragon.
- **Same proven care:** a leatherback needs exactly the same setup as any central bearded dragon.
- **Long companion:** expect 10–15 years with good care.

## Enclosure, UVB and heat

Adults need at least a 4×2×2 ft (120×60×60 cm) enclosure. Provide a T5 HO 12% desert UVB tube over the basking area, a basking surface of 100–110°F (38–43°C) and a cool side of 75–85°F (24–29°C). Our [Bearded Dragon Complete Starter Kit](/shop/enclosures/bearded-dragon-starter-kit) matches enclosure, lighting and thermostat, and our [bearded dragon care sheet](/blog/bearded-dragon-care-sheet) explains placement and distances.

Leatherbacks can be slightly more prone to dry skin and minor scrapes, so avoid very abrasive decor and offer an occasional lukewarm soak during sheds.

## Diet

Juveniles eat mostly insects (about 70%) with fresh greens daily; adults shift to around 70–80% leafy greens and vegetables with insects two to three times a week. Dust insects with calcium and use a multivitamin weekly.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the difference between a leatherback and a silkback bearded dragon?

A leatherback has one copy of the gene and reduced, smoother scales. A silkback has two copies and almost no scales, which makes it much more sensitive to UVB, dehydration and injury.

### Do leatherback bearded dragons need special care?

Not really. They need the same enclosure, UVB, heat and diet as other bearded dragons. Just avoid sharp decor and keep them well hydrated, especially during sheds.

### How big do leatherback bearded dragons get?

Like other central bearded dragons, adults reach 16–24 in (40–60 cm) including the tail and weigh 380–550 g.

### Are leatherback bearded dragons good for beginners?

Yes, for keepers who can provide a large enclosure, strong UVB and fresh greens daily. Their temperament is the same calm, handleable nature bearded dragons are known for.

name: Pinstripe Ball Python
short_description: A captive-bred pinstripe ball python with a clean tan body and fine dorsal pinstripe. Eating frozen/thawed mice and easy to handle.
long_description:
The pinstripe ball python is a classic dominant morph that replaces the normal ball python's chunky blotches with a clean, lighter body and a fine dark stripe running along the spine. It is one of the most recognizable ball python morphs, popular on its own and as a building block for combinations like the "bumblebee" (pastel pinstripe). If you want a ball python with a cleaner, more modern look but the same calm temperament, the pinstripe is a great choice.

## Pinstripe ball python at a glance

- **Look:** reduced pattern, a light brown to tan body and a thin dorsal stripe.
- **Genetics:** dominant, so one copy produces the pinstripe look.
- **Temperament:** calm and slow, like all ball pythons; they rarely bite.
- **Lifespan:** 25–30 years or more, so plan for a long friendship.

Our pinstripes are captive bred, have eaten at least four frozen/thawed meals and are handled regularly before shipping.

## Enclosure and heat

Adults do best in a 4×2×2 ft (120×60×60 cm) enclosure, ideally PVC, which holds heat and humidity well. Provide two snug hides, plenty of clutter, a warm side of 88–92°F (31–33°C) and a cool side of 76–80°F (24–27°C), with every heat source on a thermostat. Our [Ball Python Complete Starter Kit](/shop/enclosures/ball-python-starter-kit) has everything matched, and our [ball python care guide](/blog/ball-python-care-guide) covers humidity, feeding and handling in detail.

## Humidity and shedding

Keep humidity at 60–80% with a moisture-holding substrate such as cypress mulch. A humid hide helps with clean sheds.

## Feeding

Feed frozen/thawed rodents about as wide as the snake's thickest point: hopper mice for young snakes, moving to small rats as adults. Juveniles eat every 7–10 days and adults every 2–3 weeks. Healthy adults sometimes fast for weeks, which is normal as long as weight holds.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the pinstripe ball python gene healthy?

Yes. Unlike a few ball python genes associated with neurological issues, pinstripe is not linked to a "wobble" or other known health problem.

### What is a bumblebee ball python?

A bumblebee is a pastel pinstripe: a ball python carrying both the pastel and pinstripe genes, giving a bright yellow and black, heavily reduced pattern.

### How big do pinstripe ball pythons get?

The same as any ball python: usually 3–5 ft (90–150 cm), with females growing larger and heavier than males.

name: Lilly White Crested Gecko
short_description: A captive-bred Lilly White crested gecko with bright white patterning and strong crests. Eating complete diet and ready to ship.
long_description:
The Lilly White crested gecko is the most talked-about crested gecko morph of the last decade, with bright, clean white patterning that can cover the sides, back and legs. It is one of the few proven genetic crested gecko morphs, discovered by Lilly Exotics, and it has become a favorite for keepers who want a showpiece gecko with the same easy care that makes crested geckos ideal for beginners.

## About the Lilly White gene

Lilly White is an incomplete dominant gene. One copy produces the Lilly White look. Two copies (the "super" form) are not viable, so responsible breeders never pair two Lilly Whites together. If you plan to breed, pair a Lilly White with a non-Lilly White to produce roughly half Lilly White offspring. Each of our geckos is described with its visible traits; the amount of white varies between individuals and often brightens as they mature.

## Why crested geckos are so popular

- **No basking lamp in most homes:** crested geckos thrive at 72–78°F (22–26°C).
- **Simple diet:** a complete powdered crested gecko diet with insects once or twice a week.
- **Gentle:** calm once settled, with charming jumping and climbing behavior.
- **Long-lived:** 15–20 years with good care.

## Housing

Crested geckos are arboreal, so height matters. Adults need at least an 18×18×24 in enclosure, and our [Crested Gecko Complete Starter Kit](/shop/enclosures/crested-gecko-starter-kit) is a great start. Fill the enclosure with branches, cork and dense foliage, and mist each evening so humidity peaks around 70–80% before drying back to 50–60% by day. Keep temperatures below 82°F (28°C); overheating is the biggest risk with this species. Our [crested gecko care guide](/blog/crested-gecko-care-guide) explains the humidity cycle and feeding schedule.

## Feeding

Offer a [complete crested gecko diet](/shop/food-supplements/crested-gecko-diet-8oz) every other day for juveniles and three times a week for adults, plus calcium-dusted insects once or twice a week.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why can't you breed two Lilly White crested geckos together?

Pairing two Lilly Whites can produce "super Lilly White" embryos, which do not survive. Breeders pair Lilly Whites with non-Lilly White mates instead.

### Do Lilly White crested geckos need different care?

No. They have the same temperature, humidity, enclosure and diet needs as any crested gecko.

### Will my Lilly White crested gecko get whiter?

Often, yes. Crested gecko coloring develops as they grow, and many Lilly Whites show brighter, more extensive white as adults. Every gecko is different, though.

name: Eastern Blue-Tongued Skink
short_description: A captive-bred Eastern blue-tongued skink: a large, gentle, banded skink with a cobalt-blue tongue and a big personality.
long_description:
The Eastern blue-tongued skink is the largest of the Australian blue-tongued skinks and one of the most rewarding lizards you can keep. With a thick, silver-and-brown banded body, a cobalt-blue tongue and a calm, curious personality, it has become one of the fastest-growing species in the hobby. Australia does not export wildlife, so every Eastern blue-tongued skink outside Australia comes from captive breeding, and ours are hatched from established captive lines.

## Why keepers love blue-tongued skinks

- **Gentle giants:** adults reach 18–24 in (45–60 cm) but are slow, sturdy and easy to handle.
- **Omnivores:** a varied diet of vegetables, protein and some fruit, with no need for live insects every day.
- **Hardy:** forgiving of beginner mistakes compared with many lizards.
- **Long-lived:** 15–20 years or more.

## Enclosure

Adults need at least a 4×2×2 ft (120×60×60 cm) enclosure; bigger is better because skinks are active explorers. A PVC enclosure such as our [4×2×2 PVC reptile enclosure](/shop/enclosures/pvc-enclosure-4x2x2) holds heat and moderate humidity well. Provide 4–6 in of a burrowable soil, cypress or coco substrate, several hides and sturdy, low decor.

## Heat, UVB and humidity

- **Basking surface:** 95–105°F (35–41°C)
- **Cool side:** 75–80°F (24–27°C)
- **Night:** down to about 70°F (21°C)
- **Humidity:** 40–60%, with a damp hide for shedding

Use a T5 HO UVB tube (around 10–12%) over the basking area. Our [UVB lighting guide](/blog/uvb-lighting-explained) explains how far to mount it.

## Diet

Blue-tongued skinks are omnivores. A balanced plate is roughly 50% vegetables and leafy greens, 40% protein (such as high-quality skink diet, cooked lean meat, snails and insects) and up to 10% fruit. Feed juveniles every one to two days and adults two to three times a week. Dust protein foods with calcium.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do blue-tongued skinks make good pets?

Yes. They are calm, intelligent and tolerant of handling, and their omnivorous diet is simple to provide. They do need a large enclosure and proper UVB and heat.

### How big do Eastern blue-tongued skinks get?

Adults typically reach 18–24 in (45–60 cm), making them the largest blue-tongued skink species.

### Are blue-tongued skinks good for beginners?

They are a good choice for committed beginners who can provide a 4×2×2 ft enclosure. Their care is less demanding than many lizards, and they are very forgiving.

name: Red Tegu
short_description: A captive-bred red tegu (Salvator rufescens): an intelligent, dog-like lizard that colors up to rich red as it matures. For experienced keepers.
long_description:
The red tegu (*Salvator rufescens*) is a large, intelligent lizard from the dry forests and scrubland of western Argentina, Bolivia and Paraguay. Young red tegus are brown with pale bands, and males in particular develop a rich brick-red color and massive jowls as they mature. Tegus are famous for their dog-like curiosity and for becoming remarkably tame with consistent handling, which is why they are one of the fastest-rising "big lizards" in the hobby.

**Check your local laws before buying.** Tegus are restricted or require permits in some US states and countries, including Florida. We only ship to regions where keeping them is legal.

## Is a red tegu right for you?

- **Size:** adults commonly reach 3–4.5 ft (90–135 cm), with males larger than females.
- **Space:** an adult needs at least an 8×4×4 ft enclosure, so plan ahead.
- **Lifespan:** 15–20 years.
- **Temperament:** very intelligent and food-motivated; most become calm and handleable with patience.

## Enclosure and heat

Start hatchlings in a 4×2×2 ft enclosure and upgrade as they grow. Provide a basking surface of 120–130°F (49–54°C) for adults, a cool side around 75–80°F (24–27°C) and deep, moist substrate, at least 8–12 in, so they can dig a burrow. Humidity should stay around 60–80% in the substrate and burrow. Strong T5 HO UVB (around 12%) over the basking zone is essential.

Our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) explains how to create and control a very hot basking spot safely.

## Diet

Red tegus are omnivores. Feed whole prey such as rodents and chicks, plus eggs, lean meats, insects and around 10–20% fruit and vegetables. Hatchlings eat daily; adults three to four times a week. Dust non-whole-prey foods with calcium.

## Brumation

Adult tegus usually brumate (slow down and sleep) for several months in autumn and winter. This is normal; have a vet confirm your tegu is healthy before brumation begins.

## Frequently asked questions

### How big do red tegus get?

Adults usually reach 3–4.5 ft (90–135 cm). Males are larger, heavier and develop broader heads than females.

### Are red tegus friendly?

With daily, patient handling, most red tegus become very tame and even seek out interaction. Individual personalities vary, and young tegus can be flighty at first.

### Are red tegus legal to own?

It depends on where you live. Some states, including Florida, restrict or prohibit tegus. Always check your state and local regulations before buying.

### Is a red tegu a good first reptile?

Not usually. Their adult size and enclosure needs make them better suited to keepers who already have reptile experience.

name: Kimberley Rock Monitor
short_description: A captive-bred Kimberley rock monitor (Varanus glauerti): a slender, banded dwarf monitor that is active, intelligent and stunning to watch.
long_description:
The Kimberley rock monitor (*Varanus glauerti*) is a slender, semi-arboreal dwarf monitor from the rocky gorges of northwestern Australia. With a dark body crossed by pale bands, a striking ringed tail that can make up two-thirds of its length and a sharp, curious personality, it has become one of the most sought-after small monitors. Every Kimberley rock monitor sold outside Australia comes from captive breeding, and ours are hatched from established captive lines.

## Kimberley rock monitor at a glance

- **Size:** around 28–32 in (70–80 cm), mostly tail.
- **Activity:** fast, alert and very active by day. More of a "display" animal than a lap pet.
- **Lifespan:** 10–15 years or more.
- **Experience level:** intermediate to advanced; they need precise heat and humidity.

## Enclosure

Kimberley rock monitors are climbers, so height and vertical rock work matter. A single adult needs at least a 4×2×4 ft enclosure with stacked rock or cork stacks, tight crevices to hide in, sturdy climbing branches and a deep substrate of soil and sand that holds moisture lower down. PVC enclosures retain heat and humidity well.

## Heat, UVB and humidity

- **Basking surface:** 130–150°F (54–66°C) on a rock under strong halogen heat
- **Ambient warm side:** 85–90°F (29–32°C)
- **Cool side:** 75–80°F (24–27°C)
- **UVB:** T5 HO 12% over the basking area
- **Humidity:** 50–70%, with a damp burrow layer and daily light misting

Although they come from a dry region, these monitors dehydrate easily. Keep the lower substrate moist and provide a water dish large enough to soak in. Our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) and [humidity guide](/blog/reptile-humidity-guide) cover the setup.

## Diet

Kimberley rock monitors are insectivores. Feed a variety of gut-loaded roaches, crickets, superworms and black soldier fly larvae daily for juveniles and four to five times a week for adults, dusted with calcium. Occasional pinkie mice or egg can be added for adults.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Kimberley rock monitors good pets?

They are fascinating, intelligent display animals and can become tolerant of handling, but they are active and fast. They suit keepers who enjoy watching natural behavior more than frequent handling.

### How big do Kimberley rock monitors get?

Adults usually reach 28–32 in (70–80 cm), with about two-thirds of that length being tail, making them one of the smaller monitor species.

### What do Kimberley rock monitors eat?

Mainly insects: roaches, crickets, superworms and black soldier fly larvae, dusted with calcium, with occasional small rodents or egg for adults.

name: Rankin's Dragon (Dwarf Bearded Dragon)
short_description: A captive-bred Rankin's dragon, the dwarf bearded dragon: all the personality of a bearded dragon in a smaller, easier-to-house size.
long_description:
The Rankin's dragon (*Pogona henrylawsoni*), often called the dwarf bearded dragon or Lawson's dragon, is a smaller cousin of the central bearded dragon from the black-soil plains of Queensland, Australia. It reaches only 10–12 in (25–30 cm) including the tail, has a shorter, rounder head and a less spiky beard, and shares the same calm, curious temperament. For keepers who love bearded dragons but have less space, a Rankin's dragon is a superb choice.

## Rankin's dragon vs bearded dragon

| | Rankin's dragon | Central bearded dragon |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Adult size | 10–12 in (25–30 cm) | 16–24 in (40–60 cm) |
| Minimum enclosure | 36×18×18 in | 4×2×2 ft |
| Temperament | Calm, social with people | Calm, social with people |
| Lifespan | 8–12 years | 10–15 years |

## Housing

A single adult Rankin's dragon does well in a 36×18×18 in enclosure, though bigger is always welcome. Some keepers house small groups of females in larger enclosures, but males should never be kept together. A natural sand, soil and clay mix allows digging, and flat rocks under the basking light give a solid basking surface.

## Heat and UVB

- **Basking surface:** 100–105°F (38–41°C)
- **Cool side:** 75–80°F (24–27°C)
- **Night:** down to about 65–70°F (18–21°C)
- **UVB:** a T5 HO 10–12% tube over the basking area
- **Humidity:** 30–40%

The care is essentially a scaled-down version of bearded dragon care, so our [bearded dragon care sheet](/blog/bearded-dragon-care-sheet) is a useful companion guide. Use a dimming thermostat on the basking bulb and check surface temperatures with an infrared thermometer.

## Diet

Rankin's dragons are omnivores. Juveniles eat mostly small insects such as crickets, dubia roaches and black soldier fly larvae, with finely chopped greens daily. Adults eat a more balanced mix, around half greens and half insects. Dust insects with calcium and use a multivitamin weekly.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a Rankin's dragon the same as a bearded dragon?

No. It is a separate, smaller species (*Pogona henrylawsoni*) in the same genus as the central bearded dragon (*Pogona vitticeps*), with very similar care.

### How big do Rankin's dragons get?

Adults reach about 10–12 in (25–30 cm) including the tail, roughly half the size of a central bearded dragon.

### Can Rankin's dragons live together?

Males must be housed separately. Small groups of females can sometimes share a large enclosure, but watch closely for competition over food and basking spots.

name: Sunglow Corn Snake
short_description: A captive-bred sunglow corn snake: a vivid orange amelanistic corn snake with reduced white, for a glowing sunset look.
long_description:
The sunglow corn snake is one of the brightest corn snake morphs, with deep orange saddles on an orange background and very little white between them. A sunglow is an amelanistic (no black pigment) corn snake selectively bred to minimize the white borders around the saddles, so the whole snake seems to glow. Like all corn snakes, it is calm, hardy and one of the best snakes you can choose as a first pet.

## Sunglow corn snake at a glance

- **Look:** vibrant orange and red-orange with reduced white and red eyes.
- **Genetics:** amelanistic (recessive) plus line-bred reduced white.
- **Size:** 3–5 ft (90–150 cm), slender.
- **Lifespan:** 15–20 years or more.
- **Temperament:** docile and curious; rarely bites once settled.

Our sunglows are captive bred and have eaten at least four frozen/thawed pinky mice before shipping.

## Enclosure

An adult corn snake does best in a 4×2×2 ft (120×60×60 cm) enclosure with secure, locking doors, because corn snakes are famous escape artists. Provide at least two hides, branches for climbing, a few inches of burrowable substrate such as aspen or a soil mix, and a water dish large enough to soak in. Hatchlings feel safer in a smaller enclosure or a larger one packed with cover.

## Heat and humidity

- **Basking surface:** 85–90°F (29–32°C)
- **Cool side:** 70–75°F (21–24°C)
- **Night:** 65–72°F (18–22°C)
- **Humidity:** 40–60%, a little higher before a shed

Use a basking bulb on a dimming thermostat, and check temperatures with a digital thermometer. Our [corn snake care guide](/blog/corn-snake-care-guide) covers the full setup.

## Feeding

Feed frozen/thawed mice about as wide as the snake's thickest point: pinkies every 5–7 days for hatchlings, moving up to adult mice every 10–14 days for adults. Thaw prey in the fridge and warm it in hot water before offering with tongs.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the difference between a sunglow and an amelanistic corn snake?

Both lack black pigment. A sunglow is an amelanistic line selectively bred for reduced white, so it looks more uniformly orange than a typical amel with white saddle borders.

### Do sunglow corn snakes keep their color?

Yes. Most sunglows stay bright orange as adults, and many become more intense as they grow.

### Are sunglow corn snakes good for beginners?

Absolutely. They have the same easy care and docile temperament as any corn snake, which makes them one of the best first snakes.

name: Colombian Red-Tailed Boa
short_description: A captive-bred baby Colombian red-tailed boa (Boa imperator): a calm, heavy-bodied boa constrictor with rich red tail saddles. Feeding on frozen/thawed.
long_description:
Looking for a boa constrictor for sale that grows into a calm, impressive display snake? The Colombian red-tailed boa (*Boa imperator*) is the classic "BCI" boa of the pet trade: tan to silver with dark saddles that turn brick red toward the tail. Captive-bred Colombian boas are famous for their steady temperament, strong feeding response and easy handling, which makes them the most popular first large snake.

## Colombian boa at a glance

- **Size:** males 5–7 ft, females 7–9 ft (rarely 10 ft), heavy-bodied
- **Lifespan:** 25–30+ years with good care
- **Temperament:** calm and tolerant of handling once settled
- **Activity:** mostly nocturnal; uses both the floor and low branches
- **Care level:** intermediate, mainly because of adult size

Every baby boa we ship is captive bred, has shed cleanly and has eaten at least four frozen/thawed meals before it leaves us.

## Enclosure

A baby boa starts well in a 3×2×2 ft (90×60×60 cm) enclosure. Adults need at least a 6×2×2 ft (180×60×60 cm) enclosure, and large females appreciate 6×3×3 ft. PVC enclosures hold heat and humidity far better than glass. Give two snug hides, a sturdy climbing branch, a heavy water bowl big enough to soak in and 3–4 in of a humidity-holding substrate such as cypress mulch or a soil mix.

## Heat and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 88–92°F (31–33°C)
- **Cool side:** 75–80°F (24–27°C)
- **Night:** no lower than 75°F (24°C)
- **Humidity:** 55–70%, a little higher before a shed

Use a radiant heat panel or a basking bulb on a thermostat and check the gradient with a digital thermometer. Our [reptile heating guide](/blog/reptile-heating-guide) explains how to build a safe thermal gradient.

## Feeding

Feed frozen/thawed prey about as wide as the boa's thickest point: hopper mice or rat pups every 7–10 days for babies, moving to weaned and small rats every 2–4 weeks for adults. Boas are prone to obesity, so feed adults sparingly and watch body condition.

## Frequently asked questions

### How big does a Colombian red-tailed boa get?

Most males reach 5–7 ft and females 7–9 ft. They are heavy-bodied, so even a 7 ft boa is a substantial snake that needs a large enclosure as an adult.

### Is a red-tailed boa good for beginners?

A Colombian boa is a great first large snake for a keeper who is ready for its adult size. They are calm, eat reliably and are forgiving of small husbandry mistakes, but you need room for a 6 ft enclosure.

### What is the difference between a Colombian boa and a true red-tailed boa?

Colombian boas (*Boa imperator*) are the common "BCI" in the pet trade. "True red-tails" are South American *Boa constrictor constrictor*, which grow larger and need higher humidity. Ours are Colombian boas.

### How much does a Colombian red-tailed boa cost?

Normal Colombian boas usually cost $150–$300 depending on age and locality; designer morphs cost more. Our captive-bred babies are priced on this page with overnight shipping quoted at checkout.

name: Dumeril's Boa
short_description: A captive-bred Dumeril's boa from Madagascar: an exceptionally calm, slow-moving ground boa with a stunning earth-toned pattern.
long_description:
The Dumeril's boa (*Acrantophis dumerili*) is a ground-dwelling boa from southern Madagascar, and one of the gentlest large snakes you can keep. Its intricate pattern of browns, grays, pinks and black looks like a forest floor, and its relaxed, slow personality makes it a favorite with families and first-time boa keepers. If you want a Dumeril's boa for sale that is captive bred and already eating, you're in the right place.

## Dumeril's boa at a glance

- **Size:** 5–6 ft (150–180 cm), occasionally 7 ft, thick-bodied
- **Lifespan:** 20–30+ years
- **Temperament:** famously docile and slow to react
- **Activity:** terrestrial; loves to burrow under substrate and hides
- **Care level:** beginner to intermediate

All Dumeril's boas sold in the US must be captive bred (the species is CITES Appendix I), so every animal we offer comes from documented captive breeding.

## Enclosure

Babies do well in a 3×2×2 ft enclosure. Adults need floor space more than height: a 6×2×2 ft (180×60×60 cm) PVC or wooden enclosure is ideal. Provide 3–4 in of soil or cypress mulch for burrowing, two large hides, a heavy water bowl and plenty of cover such as cork bark and leaf litter.

## Heat and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 88–90°F (31–32°C)
- **Cool side:** 75–80°F (24–27°C)
- **Night:** 72–78°F (22–26°C)
- **Humidity:** 50–60%, raised to 70% during a shed

Heat from above with a basking bulb or radiant heat panel controlled by a thermostat.

## Feeding

Feed frozen/thawed mice or rat pups every 7–10 days to young boas, and appropriately sized rats every 3–4 weeks to adults. Dumeril's boas have a slow metabolism and can go off food in winter; this is normal for a healthy adult.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Dumeril's boas good pets?

Yes. They are among the calmest boas in the hobby, rarely bite and are easy to handle, making them excellent pets for patient keepers who have space for a 6 ft enclosure.

### Do Dumeril's boas need high humidity?

No. Moderate humidity of 50–60% is enough most of the time, which makes them easier to keep than many tropical boas.

### Is it legal to own a Dumeril's boa?

Captive-bred Dumeril's boas are legal to own in most US states. Because they are CITES Appendix I, interstate sales require captive-bred animals and appropriate paperwork, which we provide.

### How much does a Dumeril's boa cost?

Captive-bred Dumeril's boas typically cost $250–$450 depending on size and lineage.

name: Jungle Carpet Python
short_description: A captive-bred jungle carpet python with high-contrast black and yellow banding: an active, semi-arboreal python for keepers ready for a step up.
long_description:
The jungle carpet python (*Morelia spilota cheynei*) is one of the most striking pythons in the world: bold black and bright yellow banding on a slender, muscular body. Jungle carpets come from the rainforests of northeastern Queensland, Australia, and they are active, alert snakes that climb, explore and put on a show. Our jungle carpet pythons for sale are captive bred from high-contrast parents.

## Jungle carpet python at a glance

- **Size:** 5–7 ft (150–210 cm), slender
- **Lifespan:** 20–30 years
- **Temperament:** can be nippy as babies; most calm down with regular, gentle handling
- **Activity:** semi-arboreal and active, especially at dusk
- **Care level:** intermediate

## Enclosure

Young carpets feel secure in a 3×2×2 ft enclosure with plenty of cover. Adults need at least a 4×2×3 ft (120×60×90 cm) enclosure, and a 6×2×3 ft is better. Height matters: add sturdy horizontal branches and a raised shelf near the heat source, plus hides on the floor and up high.

## Heat and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 88–92°F (31–33°C)
- **Cool side:** 75–80°F (24–27°C)
- **Night:** 70–75°F (21–24°C)
- **Humidity:** 50–70%

Use an overhead basking bulb or heat panel on a thermostat, with a guard so the snake can't wrap around the bulb. Low-level [UVB lighting](/blog/uvb-lighting-explained) benefits carpet pythons, which bask in the open.

## Feeding

Feed frozen/thawed mice every 7 days to babies, moving up to small and medium rats every 2–3 weeks for adults. Jungle carpets have a strong feeding response, so use tongs and let the snake strike the prey.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are jungle carpet pythons aggressive?

Babies are often defensive and may nip, but most jungle carpets become calm and tolerant with consistent handling over their first year.

### How big do jungle carpet pythons get?

Jungle carpets usually reach 5–7 ft. They are slender for their length compared with ball pythons or boas.

### Do carpet pythons need a tall enclosure?

Yes. They are semi-arboreal and use height, so a 2–3 ft tall enclosure with secure branches suits them best.

### How much does a jungle carpet python cost?

Jungle carpet pythons usually sell for $200–$400; high-contrast lines and morphs cost more.

name: Children's Python
short_description: A captive-bred Children's python: a small, hardy Australian python that stays around 3 ft and is one of the easiest pythons to keep.
long_description:
The Children's python (*Antaresia childreni*) is a small Australian python named after the 19th-century naturalist John George Children, not because it's meant for kids. Still, it's one of the best small pythons for beginners: it stays around 3 ft, eats reliably, tolerates handling well and fits in a modest enclosure. If you want a python but don't have room for a large snake, a captive-bred Children's python is a great choice.

## Children's python at a glance

- **Size:** 2.5–3.5 ft (75–105 cm)
- **Lifespan:** 20–30 years
- **Temperament:** calm and curious; young ones may musk or nip but settle quickly
- **Activity:** nocturnal, active explorer
- **Care level:** beginner

## Enclosure

An adult Children's python lives comfortably in a 3×2×2 ft (90×60×60 cm) enclosure, or a 4×2×2 ft for extra enrichment. Provide two hides, a climbing branch, a water bowl and a dry, burrowable substrate such as aspen, cypress mulch or a soil mix.

## Heat and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 88–92°F (31–33°C)
- **Cool side:** 75–80°F (24–27°C)
- **Night:** 70–75°F (21–24°C)
- **Humidity:** 40–60%

Heat from above with a basking bulb or heat panel on a thermostat. See our [reptile humidity guide](/blog/reptile-humidity-guide) for tips on keeping humidity steady.

## Feeding

Hatchlings eat frozen/thawed pinky mice every 5–7 days. Adults eat an adult mouse or small rat every 10–14 days. Children's pythons are famously good eaters.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Children's pythons good for beginners?

Yes. They are small, hardy and calm, and they are one of the easiest pythons to care for, a great alternative to a ball python if you want a more active snake.

### How big do Children's pythons get?

Most adults are 2.5–3.5 ft long and only about as thick as a broom handle.

### What is the difference between Children's and spotted pythons?

They are close relatives in the genus *Antaresia*. Children's pythons have a faded, softer pattern, while spotted pythons have bold, high-contrast blotches and grow slightly larger.

### How much does a Children's python cost?

Captive-bred Children's pythons usually cost $150–$250.

### Are spotted pythons good pets?

Babies can be defensive. With short, regular handling sessions most become calm adults that rarely bite.

name: Brazilian Rainbow Boa
short_description: A captive-bred Brazilian rainbow boa with deep orange color and an iridescent sheen that shimmers in every color of the rainbow under light.
long_description:
The Brazilian rainbow boa (*Epicrates cenchria*) is one of the most beautiful snakes in the world. Its rich orange-red body with black rings is covered in microscopic ridges that split light into a shimmering rainbow sheen. Brazilian rainbow boas are medium-sized, calm as adults and very rewarding to keep, as long as you can provide the high humidity they need.

## Brazilian rainbow boa at a glance

- **Size:** 4–6 ft (120–180 cm)
- **Lifespan:** 20–30 years
- **Temperament:** babies can be nippy; adults are usually calm and handleable
- **Activity:** nocturnal; spends time on the ground and on low branches
- **Care level:** intermediate (humidity is the key)

## Enclosure

Start babies in a smaller enclosure packed with cover, then move adults into a 4×2×2 ft or 6×2×2 ft (120–180×60×60 cm) enclosure. PVC enclosures hold humidity best. Use 3–4 in of a moisture-holding substrate such as cypress mulch or [bioactive soil](/shop/substrate-decor/bioactive-soil-tropical-8qt), with a humid hide, branches and a large water bowl.

## Heat and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 85–90°F (29–32°C)
- **Cool side:** 75–80°F (24–27°C)
- **Night:** 72–76°F (22–24°C)
- **Humidity:** 75–90%

Humidity is the most important part of rainbow boa care: low humidity causes stuck sheds and respiratory problems. Our [reptile humidity guide](/blog/reptile-humidity-guide) explains how to hold it steady.

## Feeding

Feed frozen/thawed mice every 5–7 days to babies and appropriately sized rats every 10–14 days to adults.

## Frequently asked questions

### Why are they called rainbow boas?

Their scales have tiny ridges that act like prisms, so they shimmer with rainbow colors in sunlight or under bright light.

### Are Brazilian rainbow boas good for beginners?

They suit a beginner who is willing to keep humidity high. Their temperament as adults is good, but they are less forgiving of dry conditions than a corn snake or ball python.

### How big do Brazilian rainbow boas get?

Most adults are 4–6 ft long and medium-bodied.

### How much does a Brazilian rainbow boa cost?

Captive-bred Brazilian rainbow boas usually cost $200–$400.

name: Gray-Banded Kingsnake
short_description: A captive-bred gray-banded kingsnake: a small, gentle desert kingsnake with silver-gray bands and orange accents. Eating pinky mice.
long_description:
The gray-banded kingsnake (*Lampropeltis alterna*) is a small, secretive kingsnake from the Trans-Pecos deserts of Texas and northern Mexico. Prized by collectors for its huge range of looks, from silver-gray "alterna" phases to orange-saddled "Blair's" phases, it's one of the most gentle kingsnakes and rarely bites. Our captive-bred gray-banded kingsnakes are already established on frozen/thawed pinky mice, which is the hardest part with this species.

## Gray-banded kingsnake at a glance

- **Size:** 2–3 ft (60–90 cm), slender
- **Lifespan:** 15–20+ years
- **Temperament:** shy and gentle; very rarely bites
- **Activity:** nocturnal; hides during the day
- **Care level:** intermediate (hatchlings can be picky eaters)

## Enclosure

An adult lives well in a 3×1.5×1.5 ft or 3×2×2 ft (90×60×60 cm) enclosure with secure doors. Give several tight hides, rock piles or cork flats, a small water dish and a dry substrate such as aspen or a sand and soil mix.

## Heat and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 85–88°F (29–31°C)
- **Cool side:** 72–78°F (22–26°C)
- **Night:** 65–72°F (18–22°C)
- **Humidity:** 30–50%

## Feeding

Feed frozen/thawed pinky or fuzzy mice every 5–7 days to juveniles and an adult mouse every 10–14 days to adults. In the wild they eat lizards, so a picky individual may need prey scented with lizard; ours are already taking unscented mice.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are gray-banded kingsnakes good pets?

Yes, for keepers who enjoy a shy, beautiful snake. Adults are gentle and easy to keep; the main challenge is getting hatchlings eating mice, which we have already done.

### How big do gray-banded kingsnakes get?

They stay small, usually 2–3 ft long.

### Do gray-banded kingsnakes need brumation?

Pet gray-banded kingsnakes don't need brumation unless you plan to breed them.

### How much does a gray-banded kingsnake cost?

Captive-bred gray-banded kingsnakes usually cost $150–$350 depending on locality and phase.

short_description: A captive-bred leucistic Texas rat snake: pure white with striking blue eyes. A hardy, active and easy-to-feed snake for beginners.
long_description:
The leucistic Texas rat snake (*Pantherophis obsoletus lindheimeri*) is a pure white snake with striking blue-gray eyes, one of the most eye-catching snakes you can own for the price. ## Leucistic Texas rat snake at a glance

- **Size:** 4–6 ft (120–180 cm)
- **Lifespan:** 15–20+ years
- **Temperament:** alert and active; babies can be defensive but tame down well
- **Activity:** active climber, often out during the day
- **Care level:** beginner

An adult needs at least a 4×2×2 ft (120×60×60 cm) enclosure; a 4×2×3 ft lets it climb. Rat snakes are strong escape artists, so use locking doors. Add sturdy branches, hides at floor level and up high, a water bowl and a burrowable substrate such as aspen or a soil mix.

Feed frozen/thawed mice every 5–7 days to babies and adult mice or small rats every 10–14 days to adults.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is a leucistic Texas rat snake an albino?

No. Leucistic snakes lack pigment in their skin but keep dark eye pigment, so they have blue or gray eyes. Albinos have red or pink eyes.

### Are Texas rat snakes good for beginners?

Yes. They are hardy, eat well and tolerate a wide range of conditions. Babies can be nippy, but regular, gentle handling usually calms them.

### How big do leucistic Texas rat snakes get?

Most adults reach 4–6 ft.

name: Frilled Dragon
short_description: A captive-bred frilled dragon (frilled lizard): the iconic Australasian lizard that flares a huge neck frill. Active, arboreal and full of personality.
long_description:
The frilled dragon, also called the frilled lizard or frill-necked lizard (*Chlamydosaurus kingii*), is one of the most recognizable reptiles on earth. When startled, it opens a huge, colorful frill around its neck, stands up and hisses. Day to day, captive-bred frilled dragons are curious, active lizards that bask, climb and watch everything going on around them. Our frilled dragons for sale are captive bred from healthy, established adults.

## Frilled dragon at a glance

- **Size:** 2–3 ft (60–90 cm) including the tail; males larger than females
- **Lifespan:** 10–20 years
- **Temperament:** alert; tolerates handling but prefers to be watched
- **Activity:** diurnal and arboreal; spends most of its time on vertical branches
- **Care level:** intermediate

## Enclosure

Frilled dragons need height. An adult needs at least a 4×2×4 ft (120×60×120 cm) enclosure; a pair needs more. Fill it with vertical and diagonal branches, a raised basking perch, cork tubes and live or artificial plants. Use a substrate that holds some moisture, such as a soil and sand mix.

## Heat, light and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 100–110°F (38–43°C)
- **Ambient:** 80–88°F (27–31°C)
- **Night:** 70–75°F (21–24°C)
- **Humidity:** 50–70%
- **UVB:** essential; a [T5 HO UVB tube](/shop/heating-lighting/t5-ho-uvb-12-34in) across most of the enclosure

## Feeding

Frilled dragons are mostly insectivores. Feed juveniles gut-loaded crickets, dubia roaches and black soldier fly larvae daily, and adults every 2–3 days, with occasional pinky mice or greens for some adults. Dust insects with [calcium with D3](/shop/food-supplements/calcium-with-d3).

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you own a frilled dragon as a pet?

Yes. Captive-bred frilled dragons from New Guinea and Australian lines are legal to own in most US states and make fascinating pets for keepers ready for a tall, hot enclosure.

### Do frilled dragons open their frill often?

Only when startled or displaying. A well-settled frilled dragon rarely flares its frill, so don't expect to see it every day.

### How big do frilled dragons get?

Most adults reach 2–3 ft including the long tail.

### How much does a frilled dragon cost?

Captive-bred frilled dragons usually cost $350–$700 depending on locality and color.

name: Chinese Water Dragon
short_description: A captive-bred Chinese water dragon: a bright green, semi-aquatic lizard that becomes tame and handleable when raised from a baby.
long_description:
The Chinese water dragon (*Physignathus cocincinus*), also called the green water dragon, is a striking bright green lizard from the rainforests of Southeast Asia. Water dragons love to climb, bask and swim, and captive-bred babies grow into calm, handleable adults. Most water dragons in pet stores are wild-caught and stressed; ours are captive bred, which makes a huge difference to health and temperament.

## Chinese water dragon at a glance

- **Size:** males 2.5–3 ft (75–90 cm), females 2 ft (60 cm), mostly tail
- **Lifespan:** 10–15 years
- **Temperament:** captive-bred dragons tame well with regular handling
- **Activity:** diurnal, arboreal and semi-aquatic
- **Care level:** intermediate

## Enclosure

An adult needs a tall enclosure of at least 4×2×4 ft (120×60×120 cm), with a 6 ft enclosure ideal for a male. Provide climbing branches, live or artificial plants, a large water area deep enough to swim in, and a humidity-holding substrate such as coco fiber or bioactive soil. Clear glass can stress new water dragons, so cover the lower part of the front at first.

## Heat, light and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 90–95°F (32–35°C)
- **Ambient:** 80–85°F (27–29°C)
- **Night:** 72–78°F (22–26°C)
- **Humidity:** 60–80%
- **UVB:** required; a T5 HO UVB tube across the top of the enclosure

## Feeding

Feed juveniles gut-loaded insects daily and adults every 2–3 days: crickets, dubia roaches, black soldier fly larvae and the occasional earthworm. Dust feeders with calcium and a multivitamin.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Chinese water dragons good pets?

Yes, for keepers who can provide a tall, humid enclosure with water. Captive-bred water dragons become very tame and are a great step up from a bearded dragon.

### How big do Chinese water dragons get?

Males reach about 3 ft and females about 2 ft, with two-thirds of that length in the tail.

### Do Chinese water dragons need a pool?

They need a water area large enough to submerge in. They drink from it, swim and use it to stay hydrated and shed well.

### How much does a Chinese water dragon cost?

Captive-bred Chinese water dragons usually cost $90–$180; wild-caught imports cost less but are often stressed and parasitized.

name: Green Iguana
short_description: A captive-bred baby green iguana: a large, intelligent herbivorous lizard for experienced keepers ready for a room-sized enclosure.
long_description:
The green iguana (*Iguana iguana*) is the most famous pet lizard in the world, and one of the most misunderstood. Baby iguanas are small and bright green, but they grow into 5–6 ft lizards that need a room-sized enclosure, UVB, high heat and a fresh vegetable diet every day. For prepared keepers, an iguana is an intelligent, long-lived companion that can become very tame. Our baby green iguanas for sale are captive bred and already eating greens.

## Green iguana at a glance

- **Size:** 4–6 ft (120–180 cm) including tail; males larger
- **Lifespan:** 15–20+ years
- **Temperament:** can become very tame with daily handling; adult males may be territorial in breeding season
- **Activity:** diurnal and arboreal
- **Care level:** advanced, because of adult size

## Enclosure

A baby can start in a 4×2×4 ft (120×60×120 cm) enclosure, but an adult needs a custom enclosure of at least 8×4×6 ft (240×120×180 cm) or a dedicated room. Provide thick climbing branches, shelves at different heights and a large water container.

## Heat, light and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 95–100°F (35–38°C)
- **Ambient:** 80–85°F (27–29°C)
- **Night:** 75–80°F (24–27°C)
- **Humidity:** 60–80%
- **UVB:** strong UVB is essential to prevent metabolic bone disease; see [UVB lighting explained](/blog/uvb-lighting-explained)

## Feeding

Iguanas are strict herbivores. Feed a fresh salad every day of dark leafy greens (collard, mustard and turnip greens, dandelion), squash and green beans, with fruit as an occasional treat. Never feed insects or animal protein. Dust salads with calcium a few times a week.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are green iguanas good for beginners?

Not usually. Babies are easy, but adults need a very large enclosure, strong UVB and daily fresh food. We recommend iguanas for keepers who have already kept lizards and are ready for the commitment.

### How big do green iguanas get?

Most adults reach 4–6 ft including the tail and weigh 10–17 lb.

### Where can't you ship a green iguana?

Green iguanas are prohibited in Florida, and some cities and counties restrict them. Check your local laws before ordering; we will not ship to areas where they are prohibited.

### How much does a green iguana cost?

Baby green iguanas usually cost $40–$80. The enclosure, lighting and heating cost far more than the animal.

name: Eastern Collared Lizard
short_description: A captive-bred eastern collared lizard with vivid blue-green and yellow coloring and bold black collar bands. Fast, bold and very active.
long_description:
The eastern collared lizard (*Crotaphytus collaris*) is one of the most colorful lizards in North America. Males can be turquoise, green or blue with yellow heads, crossed by two bold black collar bands. Collared lizards are famous for sprinting on their hind legs, and in captivity they are bold, active lizards that bask in the open and are always on the move. Our collared lizards for sale are captive bred, not wild collected.

## Collared lizard at a glance

- **Size:** 8–14 in (20–35 cm) including tail
- **Lifespan:** 5–10 years in captivity
- **Temperament:** bold and alert; better for watching than heavy handling
- **Activity:** diurnal, terrestrial and very active
- **Care level:** intermediate

## Enclosure

A single adult needs at least a 4×2×2 ft (120×60×60 cm) enclosure, because collared lizards are fast and need running room. Use a deep arid substrate such as a soil and sand mix, stacked and secured rocks for basking, and several hides.

## Heat, light and humidity

- **Basking surface:** 105–115°F (41–46°C)
- **Ambient:** 80–90°F (27–32°C) warm side, 75–80°F (24–27°C) cool side
- **Night:** 65–75°F (18–24°C)
- **Humidity:** 20–40%
- **UVB:** essential; a [T5 HO UVB tube](/shop/heating-lighting/t5-ho-uvb-12-34in)

## Feeding

Collared lizards are insectivores with big appetites. Feed juveniles gut-loaded crickets, dubia roaches and black soldier fly larvae daily and adults every 1–2 days, dusted with calcium and a multivitamin.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are collared lizards good pets?

Yes, for keepers who enjoy an active display lizard. They are hardy and fascinating to watch, but they are fast and prefer minimal handling.

### Do collared lizards need UVB?

Yes. They are sun-loving desert lizards and need strong UVB and a very hot basking spot to stay healthy.

### How big do collared lizards get?

Adults reach 8–14 in including the tail; males are larger and more colorful.

### How much does a collared lizard cost?

Captive-bred collared lizards usually cost $70–$150.

name: Red-Eyed Crocodile Skink
short_description: A captive-bred red-eyed crocodile skink: a tiny 'dragon' with armored scales and orange eye rings. Shy, humid-loving and fascinating.
long_description:
The red-eyed crocodile skink (*Tribolonotus gracilis*) looks like a miniature dragon: rows of armored, crocodile-like scales, a bony head and bright orange rings around its eyes. These small skinks from New Guinea are shy and secretive, live in humid leaf litter and even "chirp" when handled. A captive-bred red-eyed crocodile skink is a rewarding display animal for a humid bioactive terrarium.

## Red-eyed crocodile skink at a glance

- **Size:** 7–9 in (18–23 cm) including tail
- **Lifespan:** 10–15 years
- **Temperament:** shy; may freeze or vocalize when handled; best as a display animal
- **Activity:** crepuscular; most active at dawn and dusk
- **Care level:** intermediate

## Enclosure

One or two skinks live well in an 18×18×12 in or a 24×18×18 in (60×45×45 cm) terrarium. Floor space matters more than height. Use a deep, damp [bioactive soil](/shop/substrate-decor/bioactive-soil-tropical-8qt) topped with [leaf litter](/shop/substrate-decor/leaf-litter-mix) and moss, several hides and a shallow water dish they can soak in. See [how to set up a bioactive terrarium](/blog/how-to-set-up-a-bioactive-terrarium).

## Heat and humidity

- **Warm side:** 78–82°F (26–28°C), no hot basking spot
- **Cool side:** 72–76°F (22–24°C)
- **Night:** 68–72°F (20–22°C)
- **Humidity:** 70–90%

These skinks overheat easily, so avoid hot basking bulbs; a low-wattage heat source on a thermostat is enough.

## Feeding

Feed small gut-loaded crickets, dubia roaches, black soldier fly larvae and earthworms every 2–3 days, dusted with calcium.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you handle red-eyed crocodile skinks?

Occasionally and gently, but they are shy and may freeze, play dead or squeak. They do best as display animals.

### Do red-eyed crocodile skinks need UVB?

Low-level UVB is beneficial in a planted enclosure with plenty of shade, but the most important needs are high humidity and moderate temperatures.

### How big do crocodile skinks get?

Adults reach 7–9 in including the tail.

### How much does a red-eyed crocodile skink cost?

Captive-bred red-eyed crocodile skinks usually cost $90–$180.

name: Tokay Gecko
short_description: A captive-bred tokay gecko: a large, vividly blue and orange-spotted gecko famous for its loud 'to-kay' call. Bold and hardy.
long_description:
The tokay gecko (*Gekko gecko*) is a large, striking gecko from Southeast Asia, with blue-gray skin covered in orange and red spots and big golden eyes. Tokays are named after their loud "to-kay" call, and they are famous for their attitude: a tokay will stand its ground, gape and bite if it feels cornered. In return, they are extremely hardy, live a long time and are spectacular display animals. Our tokay geckos for sale are captive bred, so they are healthier and calmer than wild-caught imports.

## Tokay gecko at a glance

- **Size:** 10–14 in (25–35 cm)
- **Lifespan:** 10–20 years
- **Temperament:** defensive and vocal; best as a display animal
- **Activity:** nocturnal and arboreal
- **Care level:** intermediate

## Enclosure

An adult tokay needs a vertical enclosure of at least 18×18×24 in (45×45×60 cm), and an [18×18×36 in arboreal terrarium](/shop/enclosures/glass-terrarium-18x18x36-arboreal) is better. Fill it with cork bark tubes and flats for hiding, branches and plants. A humidity-holding substrate such as coco fiber or bioactive soil works well.

## Heat and humidity

- **Warm side:** 85–90°F (29–32°C)
- **Cool side:** 75–80°F (24–27°C)
- **Night:** 70–75°F (21–24°C)
- **Humidity:** 60–80%, mist every evening

## Feeding

Feed juveniles gut-loaded crickets, dubia roaches and other insects every day or two, and adults every 2–3 days. Dust feeders with calcium and a multivitamin.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do tokay geckos bite?

They can, and their bite is strong for a gecko. Captive-bred tokays are usually calmer than wild-caught ones, but they are best treated as display animals rather than handled pets.

### Why are they called tokay geckos?

Males make a loud, two-part "to-kay" call, especially at night during the breeding season.

### How big do tokay geckos get?

Adults usually reach 10–14 in, making them one of the largest geckos in the pet trade.

### How much does a tokay gecko cost?

Captive-bred tokay geckos usually cost $50–$120; color morphs such as granite or powder blue cost more.

name: New Caledonian Giant Gecko (Leachianus)
short_description: A captive-bred Rhacodactylus leachianus, the world's largest gecko: a gentle giant with moss-like camouflage and a deep growling voice.
long_description:
The New Caledonian giant gecko (*Rhacodactylus leachianus*), known to keepers as the "leachie", is the largest living gecko in the world. Leachies have soft, loose skin patterned like moss and lichen, short stumpy tails and a famous growl. They are long-lived, hardy and become calm with age, which makes them a dream gecko for many collectors. Our captive-bred leachianus geckos for sale come from established island-locality lines.

## Leachianus gecko at a glance

- **Size:** 14–17 in (35–43 cm) total length
- **Lifespan:** 20+ years
- **Temperament:** babies can be defensive and vocal; most become calm adults
- **Activity:** nocturnal and arboreal
- **Care level:** intermediate

## Enclosure

A juvenile can start in an 18×18×24 in enclosure. An adult needs at least an 18×18×36 in or 24×24×48 in (60×60×120 cm) vertical enclosure with thick vertical cork tubes, sturdy branches and dense foliage. Good airflow is important, so combine a glass terrarium with a mesh top or a hybrid enclosure.

## Heat and humidity

- **Daytime:** 72–80°F (22–27°C), with a gentle warm spot up to 82°F
- **Night:** 65–72°F (18–22°C)
- **Humidity:** 60–80% at night after misting, drying out partly by day
- Avoid temperatures above 85°F (29°C)

## Feeding

Feed a complete [crested gecko diet](/shop/food-supplements/crested-gecko-diet-8oz) 3 times a week, plus gut-loaded insects such as dubia roaches once or twice a week. Many adults also enjoy the occasional pinky mouse.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the largest gecko in the world?

*Rhacodactylus leachianus*, the New Caledonian giant gecko, is the largest living gecko species, reaching up to 17 in total length.

### Are leachianus geckos good pets?

Yes, for patient keepers. They are hardy and long-lived and don't need UVB or very high heat, but babies can be defensive and the species is a significant investment.

### Do leachianus geckos make noise?

Yes. They are well known for growling and barking, especially when disturbed at night.

### How much does a leachianus gecko cost?

Captive-bred leachianus usually cost $800–$2,500 depending on locality and size.

name: Giant Day Gecko
short_description: A captive-bred giant day gecko (Phelsuma grandis): a brilliant emerald-green gecko with red markings that's active all day.
long_description:
The giant day gecko (*Phelsuma grandis*) is one of the most colorful reptiles you can keep: brilliant emerald green with red spots and stripes, active by day and always visible. Unlike most geckos, day geckos bask in the sun, lap nectar and fruit, and patrol their enclosure from morning till night. A captive-bred giant day gecko is a showstopper in a planted vivarium.

## Giant day gecko at a glance

- **Size:** 10–12 in (25–30 cm)
- **Lifespan:** 10–20 years
- **Temperament:** fast and skittish; delicate skin, so not a handling pet
- **Activity:** diurnal and arboreal
- **Care level:** intermediate

An adult needs a vertical enclosure of at least 18×18×24 in, and an [18×18×36 in arboreal terrarium](/shop/enclosures/glass-terrarium-18x18x36-arboreal) is ideal. Provide smooth vertical surfaces such as bamboo tubes, plenty of broad-leaved live plants and a [bioactive substrate](/shop/enclosures/bioactive-kit-tropical).

- **Basking spot:** 90–95°F (32–35°C)
- **Ambient:** 75–82°F (24–28°C)
- **Night:** 68–72°F (20–22°C)
- **Humidity:** 60–80%; mist morning and evening
- **UVB:** required, with a T5 HO UVB tube over part of the enclosure

## Feeding

Offer a fruit-based gecko diet such as [crested gecko diet](/shop/food-supplements/crested-gecko-diet-8oz) 2–3 times a week, plus gut-loaded crickets, roaches or black soldier fly larvae dusted with calcium. Day geckos also love a lick of fruit puree.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you handle giant day geckos?

It's best not to. Day geckos have delicate skin that can tear and they are very fast, so they are display animals.

### Do giant day geckos need UVB?

Yes. As day-active basking geckos they need UVB to make vitamin D3 and stay healthy.

### How big do giant day geckos get?

Adults reach 10–12 in, making them the largest commonly kept day gecko.

### How much does a giant day gecko cost?

Captive-bred giant day geckos usually cost $90–$200; high-red lines cost more.

name: Mourning Gecko
short_description: A captive-bred mourning gecko: a tiny, all-female gecko that reproduces without males. Ideal for small bioactive vivariums.
long_description:
The mourning gecko (*Lepidodactylus lugubris*) is a tiny, peaceful gecko with a remarkable trick: the species is almost entirely female and reproduces by parthenogenesis, laying fertile eggs without a male. Mourning geckos live happily in small groups, chirp to each other at night and are perfect for a small planted or bioactive vivarium. They are one of the easiest and most affordable geckos you can keep.

## Mourning gecko at a glance

- **Size:** 3.5–4 in (9–10 cm)
- **Lifespan:** around 10 years
- **Temperament:** peaceful; a colony animal best enjoyed as a display
- **Activity:** mostly nocturnal, often seen at dusk
- **Care level:** beginner

## Enclosure

A small group of 2–4 mourning geckos lives well in a [12×12×18 in terrarium](/shop/enclosures/glass-terrarium-12x12x18) or larger. Plant it densely and include cork bark and bamboo for hiding and egg-laying. Remember that they will breed, so plan for the colony to grow.

## Heat and humidity

- **Day:** 75–82°F (24–28°C)
- **Night:** 68–72°F (20–22°C)
- **Humidity:** 60–80%; mist daily
- **UVB:** low-level UVB is beneficial in planted vivariums

## Feeding

Offer a fruit-based gecko diet such as [crested gecko diet](/shop/food-supplements/crested-gecko-diet-8oz) 3 times a week, plus fruit flies and small crickets dusted with calcium.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do mourning geckos need a male to lay eggs?

No. Mourning geckos are parthenogenetic: females lay fertile eggs that hatch into genetic copies of the mother, so a single gecko can start a colony.

### Can mourning geckos live together?

Yes. They are one of the few geckos that do well in groups, and they communicate with soft chirps.

### Are mourning geckos good for beginners?

Very. They are small, hardy, inexpensive and easy to feed, and they thrive in small bioactive setups.

### How much does a mourning gecko cost?

Mourning geckos usually cost $20–$40 each.

short_description: A captive-bred Jackson's chameleon: the three-horned 'mini triceratops' chameleon from East Africa. Bright green and endlessly fascinating.
long_description:
The Jackson's chameleon (*Trioceros jacksonii xantholophus*) is the iconic three-horned chameleon, often called a "mini triceratops". Males carry three long horns; females have smaller or no horns. Jackson's chameleons are bright green, give birth to live young instead of laying eggs, and come from cool, misty highlands in East Africa, so they prefer milder temperatures than veiled or panther chameleons. Our Jackson's chameleons for sale are captive bred in the US.

## Jackson's chameleon at a glance

- **Size:** males 9–13 in (23–33 cm), females slightly smaller
- **Lifespan:** 5–10 years
- **Temperament:** generally calm; like all chameleons, best handled minimally
- **Activity:** diurnal and arboreal
- **Care level:** advanced

## Enclosure

Chameleons need airflow. An adult needs a [screen chameleon cage of 24×24×48 in](/shop/enclosures/screen-chameleon-cage-24x24x48) or a hybrid enclosure, packed with live plants such as pothos and ficus, horizontal branches at different heights and a dripper.

## Heat, light and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 80–85°F (27–29°C)
- **Ambient:** 70–78°F (21–26°C)
- **Night:** 55–65°F (13–18°C); a night drop is important
- **Humidity:** 50–80%, peaking at night and in the morning
- **UVB:** required; a T5 HO UVB tube across the top of the cage

Chameleons don't drink from bowls. Mist 2–3 times a day and run a dripper so they can lap water droplets from leaves; an [automatic misting system](/shop/care-accessories/automatic-misting-system) makes this easy.

## Feeding

Feed gut-loaded crickets, dubia roaches, black soldier fly larvae and silkworms. Juveniles eat daily; adults every other day. Dust with calcium and use a multivitamin twice a month.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Jackson's chameleons good for beginners?

They are best for keepers with some chameleon or reptile experience. They need cooler temperatures, a night drop and frequent misting.

### Do Jackson's chameleons lay eggs?

No. They are ovoviviparous: females give birth to 8–30 live babies after a pregnancy of about 5–6 months.

### Do female Jackson's chameleons have horns?

Female *xantholophus* usually have no horns or small nubs, while males have three prominent horns.

### How much does a Jackson's chameleon cost?

Captive-bred Jackson's chameleons usually cost $150–$300.

name: Sulcata Tortoise
short_description: A captive-bred sulcata tortoise (African spurred tortoise): a friendly, grazing tortoise that becomes one of the largest pets you can own.
long_description:
The sulcata tortoise (*Centrochelys sulcata*), or African spurred tortoise, is the third-largest tortoise in the world and one of the most popular pet tortoises in the US. Baby sulcata tortoises are small and adorable, but they grow fast and become 70–100+ lb grazers that live for decades. Sulcatas are friendly, curious and full of personality, and they are a lifelong commitment best suited to keepers with a warm climate and a large, secure yard. Our sulcata tortoises for sale are captive hatched and started on a high-fiber diet.

## Sulcata tortoise at a glance

- **Size:** 24–30 in (60–75 cm) shell length; 70–100+ lb as adults
- **Lifespan:** 70+ years
- **Temperament:** curious and friendly; strong diggers
- **Activity:** diurnal grazer
- **Care level:** intermediate (because of adult size)

## Housing

Hatchlings and young sulcatas do best indoors on a [tortoise table](/shop/enclosures/tortoise-table-48x24) or a closed chamber with a humid hide. Once they reach about 10–12 in and the climate allows, they need a large, secure outdoor pen with a heated shelter. Adults can dig deep burrows, so fences must extend below ground.

## Heat, light and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 95–100°F (35–38°C)
- **Ambient:** 80–85°F (27–29°C)
- **Night:** 70–80°F (21–27°C)
- **Humidity:** 50–70% for hatchlings, lower for adults, with a humid hide
- **UVB:** essential indoors; natural sunlight is best

## Feeding

Sulcatas are grazers. Feed mostly grasses and hay (Timothy and orchard grass), broadleaf weeds such as dandelion and plantain, and [tortoise diet pellets](/shop/food-supplements/tortoise-diet-pellets) as a supplement. Avoid fruit and high-protein foods, which cause pyramiding. Dust food with calcium and provide a shallow water dish.

## Frequently asked questions

### How big do sulcata tortoises get?

Adults usually reach 24–30 in shell length and weigh 70–100 lb, with some males exceeding 150 lb.

### How long do sulcata tortoises live?

With good care, sulcatas can live 70 years or more, so plan for them to outlive you.

### Can a sulcata tortoise live indoors?

Only while small. Adults need a large outdoor enclosure with a heated shelter for cool nights.

### How much does a baby sulcata tortoise cost?

Baby sulcata tortoises usually cost $100–$250. Housing, UVB and heating cost more than the tortoise itself.

name: Leopard Tortoise
short_description: A captive-bred leopard tortoise with a high-domed, golden shell spotted in black: a gentle, grazing tortoise from southern and eastern Africa.
long_description:
The leopard tortoise (*Stigmochelys pardalis*) is named for the beautiful black-spotted, golden pattern on its high-domed shell. It's one of the most attractive tortoises in the world, and one of the gentlest. Leopard tortoises are grazers from the savannas of southern and eastern Africa that grow to a medium-large size, smaller than a sulcata but still big enough to need an outdoor enclosure in warm months. Our leopard tortoises for sale are captive bred.

## Leopard tortoise at a glance

- **Size:** 10–18 in (25–45 cm) shell length, 20–40 lb as adults
- **Lifespan:** 50–100 years
- **Temperament:** shy at first, then calm and gentle; leopards don't dig like sulcatas
- **Activity:** diurnal grazer
- **Care level:** intermediate

## Housing

Keep young leopard tortoises indoors on a [tortoise table](/shop/enclosures/tortoise-table-48x24) or closed chamber with a humid hide. Adults need a large outdoor pen in warm weather and a heated indoor area when it's cool, as leopards are sensitive to cold and damp.

## Heat, light and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 95–100°F (35–38°C)
- **Ambient:** 80–85°F (27–29°C)
- **Night:** 70–75°F (21–24°C)
- **Humidity:** 50–70% for hatchlings, 40–60% for adults
- **UVB:** essential indoors; natural sunlight is best

## Feeding

Feed a high-fiber diet of grasses, hay, broadleaf weeds such as dandelion, plantain and clover, and edible flowers, supplemented with [tortoise diet pellets](/shop/food-supplements/tortoise-diet-pellets). Avoid fruit. Dust food with calcium.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are leopard tortoises good pets?

Yes. They are gentle and beautiful, and less destructive than sulcatas because they don't dig deep burrows. They do need warmth and plenty of space as adults.

### How big do leopard tortoises get?

Most reach 10–18 in shell length; size varies by bloodline.

### What's the difference between a leopard tortoise and a sulcata?

Leopard tortoises are smaller, have a high-domed spotted shell and don't burrow, while sulcatas grow much larger and dig.

### How much does a leopard tortoise cost?

Captive-bred baby leopard tortoises usually cost $200–$400.

name: Greek Tortoise
short_description: A captive-bred Greek tortoise (spur-thighed tortoise): a small, hardy Mediterranean tortoise that's an excellent choice for beginners.
long_description:
The Greek tortoise (*Testudo graeca*), also called the spur-thighed tortoise, is a small, hardy Mediterranean tortoise with a golden to olive shell marked in black. Greek tortoises stay a manageable size, are active and curious, and do well indoors on a tortoise table with outdoor time in warm weather. They are one of the best tortoises for beginners and families.

## Greek tortoise at a glance

- **Size:** 5–8 in (13–20 cm) shell length
- **Lifespan:** 50+ years
- **Temperament:** active, curious and hardy
- **Activity:** diurnal grazer and browser
- **Care level:** beginner

## Housing

A [48×24 in tortoise table](/shop/enclosures/tortoise-table-48x24) is the minimum for one adult; bigger is better. Use a mix of topsoil and play sand deep enough to dig, add a hide and a shallow water dish. In warm, dry weather, a secure outdoor pen with shade and a shelter is ideal.

## Heat, light and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 95–100°F (35–38°C)
- **Ambient:** 70–80°F (21–27°C)
- **Night:** 60–70°F (16–21°C)
- **Humidity:** 40–60%, with a humid hide for juveniles
- **UVB:** essential indoors; see [UVB lighting explained](/blog/uvb-lighting-explained)

## Feeding

Feed broadleaf weeds such as dandelion, plantain, clover and mallow, dark leafy greens and edible flowers, with [tortoise diet pellets](/shop/food-supplements/tortoise-diet-pellets) as an occasional supplement. Avoid fruit. Dust food with calcium.

## Frequently asked questions

### Are Greek tortoises good for beginners?

Yes. They stay small, are hardy and adapt well to life on a tortoise table with outdoor time.

### How big do Greek tortoises get?

Most adults reach 5–8 in shell length, depending on the subspecies.

### Do Greek tortoises hibernate?

Healthy adults can hibernate in winter, but it isn't required for a pet and should only be done with a healthy, well-fed tortoise and careful temperature control.

### How much does a Greek tortoise cost?

Captive-bred Greek tortoises usually cost $175–$350.

name: Marginated Tortoise
short_description: A captive-bred marginated tortoise: the largest Testudo, with a dark shell and a dramatic flared rear edge. Hardy and long-lived.
long_description:
The marginated tortoise (*Testudo marginata*) is the largest of the Mediterranean *Testudo* tortoises, native to Greece and southern Italy. Adults develop a dark, almost black shell with a dramatic flared skirt at the back, which gives the species its name. Marginated tortoises are hardy, active and long-lived, and they stay small enough to keep indoors on a large tortoise table with outdoor time in summer.

## Marginated tortoise at a glance

- **Size:** 10–14 in (25–35 cm) shell length
- **Lifespan:** 50–100 years
- **Temperament:** active and curious
- **Activity:** diurnal grazer
- **Care level:** intermediate

## Housing

Young tortoises do well on a [48×24 in tortoise table](/shop/enclosures/tortoise-table-48x24); adults need at least twice that floor space or a secure outdoor pen in warm, dry weather. Use a deep topsoil and sand mix, a hide and a shallow water dish.

## Heat, light and humidity

- **Basking spot:** 95–100°F (35–38°C)
- **Ambient:** 70–80°F (21–27°C)
- **Night:** 60–70°F (16–21°C)
- **Humidity:** 40–60%, with a humid hide for juveniles
- **UVB:** essential indoors

## Feeding

Feed a varied diet of broadleaf weeds, dark leafy greens, grasses and edible flowers, with [tortoise pellets](/shop/food-supplements/tortoise-diet-pellets) as a supplement. Avoid fruit. Dust food with calcium.

## Frequently asked questions

### How big do marginated tortoises get?

Adults usually reach 10–14 in shell length, making them the largest *Testudo* species.

### Are marginated tortoises good pets?

Yes. They are hardy, active and long-lived, and they suit keepers who can offer a large indoor table plus outdoor space in summer.

### Why does a marginated tortoise's shell flare?

The flared rear margin develops as the tortoise matures, especially in males. It's natural and one of the species' signature features.

### How much does a marginated tortoise cost?

Captive-bred marginated tortoises usually cost $250–$450.
